exception.ruling: No owner ruling is engaged, on the same reading that `D-20` was given for record 03. Nothing in `contracts/**` moved: `DecisionEvent.author_label` is declared by the seal with the same type and the same 1..128 bounds, and no property was added to any schema, so neither R-5's kind of authority (adding a property) nor R-10's (filling a declared property that had no producer) is what this is. What changed is the VALUE the server writes into a field it has always written: it was one configured constant for every reviewer and is now the login of the reviewer the authorization seam verified. The frozen document's *description* of the field still calls it "one configured local reviewer label" and is now wrong; correcting that sentence is a reseal and is the owner's, and it is reported rather than done here. **`R-37`, 2026-09-23: the label is now the reviewer's DISPLAY NAME and not their login.** The owner ruled that what other reviewers read on a decision should be a name rather than an address. This record's bytes did not move for it, and the reason is the ruling's own fallback: the account this journey provisions -- `w13-baseline` -- has chosen no display name, so `UserRecord.display_label` answers with its login, which is the same string this record already pinned. So the record still pins a true answer; what it no longer distinguishes is a seam carrying the name from one carrying the login. That distinction is asserted where it can be -- `tests/integration/api/test_decision_authorship.py`, over three accounts, two of them named something other than their login -- and it is stated here rather than left to be inferred from a record that did not change.
exception.decided_by_subject: feat(A1): D-78 -- a decision is attributed to the reviewer who made it
exception.permitted_change: `author_label` was `"local-reviewer"` -- `CONFIGURED_AUTHOR_LABEL` in `auditmanager.decisions.ledger`, one string for every verdict by every reviewer. It is now the `login` of the `Subject` the authorization seam verified for the request, which in this journey is the account `journey.static_token()` provisions: `w13-baseline`. The body is otherwise byte-identical -- same status, same headers, same properties in the same order -- and the declared length moves by the two bytes the shorter login costs. Record 11 renders the same event through `listDecisionHistory` and moves with it for the same reason; the two are one change seen twice, which is why they are separate entries rather than one. **Amended by `R-37`:** the value is the verified subject's `display_label` -- the reviewer's chosen name, or their login when they have chosen none -- and not `login`. `w13-baseline` has chosen none, so what this record pins is unchanged.
